description: How should domain concepts handle and communicate errors and exceptional conditions?
question: What is your default approach for error handling in the domain?

options.name: Exception-Based
options.description: Throw domain exceptions for error conditions. Catch and handle at appropriate layer.
options.when_to_use: Exceptional conditions are truly exceptional, framework supports exceptions, stack trace valuable

options.name: Result Objects
options.description: Return result objects that contain success/failure status and error details. No exceptions for domain errors.
options.when_to_use: Errors are expected outcomes, functional style, explicit error handling, performance sensitive
options.example: Order.Submit() returns OrderResult with: IsSuccess, Order, Errors list

options.name: Validation Collection
options.description: Collect all validation errors before failing. Return complete list of issues, not just first one.
options.when_to_use: Form validation, user input, batch processing, multiple independent validations
options.example: Order.Validate() returns ValidationResult with all errors: missing address, invalid card, out of stock items

options.name: Domain Events for Failures
options.description: Publish failure events that interested parties can subscribe to. Decoupled error handling.
options.when_to_use: Event-driven architecture, multiple error handlers, audit/logging requirements
options.example: Order publishes OrderSubmissionFailed event with reason. ErrorHandler, AuditLog, Notification subscribe

options.name: Null Object / Fallback
options.description: Return null objects or fallback values instead of errors. Operations continue with sensible defaults.
options.when_to_use: Optional data, graceful degradation, avoid null checks, chain of responsibility
options.example: Customer.GetLoyaltyTier() returns GuestTier (null object) if no tier assigned - calculations still work
